claims.claim: **ATTRv-PN is a rare autosomal dominant multisystem disease from TTR gene variants,** causing a length-dependent sensorimotor and autonomic neuropathy, often with cardiomyopathy. Untreated, it brings major disability and early death.
claims.source_text: Hereditary transthyretin (ATTRv) amyloidosis with polyneuropathy (ATTRv-PN) is a rare, autosomal dominant, multisystem disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the transthyretin (TTR) gene [, ], leading to misfolding and aggregation of TTR and subsequent extracellular deposition of amyloid fibrils []. Progressive amyloid accumulation results in a length-dependent sensorimotor and autonomic neuropathy, frequently accompanied by cardiomyopathy and other organ involvement [, -]. If left untreated, ATTRv-PN is associated with substantial morbidity and premature mortality
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Musculoskeletal red flags can precede systemic disease by years:** bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, lumbar spinal stenosis, and biceps or other large tendon rupture.
claims.source_text: Years to decades before systemic disease onset, TTR amyloid can form at different musculoskeletal sites, which results in manifestations such as (bilateral) carpal tunnel syndrome, lumbar spinal stenosis, and ruptures of biceps or other large tendons being considered a diagnostic red flag
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **TTR amyloid on a soft-tissue biopsy calls for neurological and cardiac assessment and TTR genetic testing.** If a variant is found, start treatment at the first minor sign of neuropathy; if wild-type, early cardiac signs (ECG, NT-proBNP, hs-troponin, echo) should prompt bone scintigraphy and/or cardiac MRI.
claims.source_text: The panel advises that patients with TTR amyloid (according to amyloid subtyping) in a soft tissue biopsy should undergo neurological and cardiological assessments and be genetically tested for amyloidogenic TTR variants. If positive (ATTRv), treatment should be initiated upon minor signs or symptoms of neuropathy onset. If negative (ATTRwt), the earliest signs of cardiomyopathy (e.g. ECG, NT-proBNP, high sensitive troponin, echocardiography) should prompt to tightening the diagnosis of ATTRwt by bone scan scintigraphy and/or cardiac MRI
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Exclude AL amyloidosis early with serum free light chains and immunofixation.**
claims.source_text: Importantly, AL amyloidosis should be excluded at an early stage by serum free light chain measurement and immunofixation.
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage neuropathy by Coutinho (FAP) stage:** stage 1 walks unaided, stage 2 needs walking aids, stage 3 is wheelchair-bound or bedridden.
claims.source_text: In FAP stage 1, patients are fully ambulatory, in stage 2, they use walking aids, and in stage 3, individuals are wheelchair-bound or bedridden
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat symptomatic patients with a confirmed amyloidogenic variant as early as possible.** Asymptomatic carriers have no approved preventive therapy; carriers with biopsy-proven amyloid but no disease features need close monitoring and a multidisciplinary decision.
claims.source_text: In symptomatic patients with confirmed amyloidogenic TTR variants, treatment should be initiated as early as possible [-, ]. In Germany, marketing authorizations do not require confirmation of amyloid deposits by tissue biopsy [-]. In asymptomatic TTR variant carriers, there is no approved treatment strategy to prevent disease onset … Variant carriers with histologically proven tissue amyloid deposition but no typical disease symptoms or findings of disease manifestation in an initial comprehensive set of diagnostic tests (yet) should be strictly monitored with individual treatment considerations provided by a multidisciplinary board of experts
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **First line: a second-generation silencer, vutrisiran (siRNA) or eplontersen (ASO);** neither is superior. Vutrisiran is also studied and approved for ATTR-CM.
claims.source_text: the panel recommends using one of the two second-generation RNA silencers, the small interfering RNA (siRNA) agent vutrisiran [] or the antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) eplontersen [], as first-line therapy … none of the two can be considered superior in overall efficacy. Vutrisiran has been studied and approved for ATTR-CM as well [, ], whereas the respective trial for eplontersen is still ongoing
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Patisiran (heavier burden: IV infusions with steroid premedication) and inotersen (more safety issues and monitoring) are second line.** Patients stable on patisiran who prefer to continue may stay on it.
claims.source_text: Patisiran has a significantly higher treatment burden over vutrisiran, and inotersen comes with greater safety issues and monitoring requirements; they should therefore be considered second-line options. If patients are stable under patisiran and explicitly prefer DMT continuation over DMT switch, there is no medical reasoning not to abide with the patients' preference
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tafamidis (20 mg, or 61 mg with mixed phenotype) is first choice if the patient wants oral therapy,** and first line for very early FAP1 disease with p.(Val50Met), but it is a bridge: switch to a silencer at any sign of progression. It is not approved in stage 2.
claims.source_text: If patients explicitly prefer oral over subcutaneous route of administration, tafamidis (20 mg or 61 mg in patients with mixed phenotype) would be the first choice. Since market authorization in 2012, trial and real-world data have shown that very early FAP1 patients with the p.(Val50Met) TTR variant profit best from this DMT, especially if female [, ]. With responder rates ~ 70% and very minor side effects only, tafamidis (20 mg or 61 mg in patients with mixed phenotype) can be considered as first-line therapy in these specific cohorts. However, the expert panel acknowledges tafamidis to be rather a bridging DMT with immediate switch to a more efficacious silencer upon any indication of disease progression … In stage 2, tafamidis is not approved, whereas the other DMTs remain approved for use in this stage
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diflunisal** may work as well as tafamidis but carries gastrointestinal, cardiac and renal toxicity. **Acoramidis** is approved only for ATTR-CM.
claims.source_text: Diflunisal, an orally administered non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with disease-modifying effects mediated by TTR stabilization might be equally efficacious as tafamidis [] (no head-to-head comparison available) but has a more relevant safety profile (potential gastrointestinal, cardiac, and renal toxicity) []. Acoramidis is a TTR stabilizer with enhanced binding to both thyroxine binding sites. However, it has not been studied in ATTRv-PN and is currently approved for ATTR-CM only
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dosing burden:** vutrisiran is subcutaneous every three months; eplontersen monthly by autoinjector at home; patisiran IV every three weeks with premedication; inotersen weekly subcutaneous with monitoring for thrombocytopenia and kidney harm.
claims.source_text: Tafamidis and diflunisal are administered orally, whereas patisiran requires premedication-supported intravenous infusion every three weeks and therefore access to an infusion facility. In contrast, the second-generation gene-silencing therapies vutrisiran and eplontersen are administered subcutaneously at longer intervals (every three months and once monthly, respectively), which may substantially reduce treatment burden and facilitate outpatient management. Eplontersen is available as an autoinjector that allows home-based self-administration after appropriate patient training. In certain situations, support by home-care nursing services may further facilitate treatment delivery and improve adherence. Inotersen is also administered subcutaneously once weekly and may be self-administered, but requires regular laboratory monitoring because of the risk of thrombocytopenia and renal adverse events
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor regularly for side effects and response** using a sensible combination of tests, ideally by the same trained examiner each visit; progression is any new or worsening disease-specific sign or symptom.
claims.source_text: Patients under DMT should be regularly monitored in terms of side effects and treatment response [, ]. Disease progression is defined by any additional and/or worsening signs and/or symptoms that are specific to the disease. Other than in clinical trial settings, the expert panel does not recommend using one specific score or instrument to measure progression but to choose a reasonable combination of tests conducted by trained examiners who should, ideally, be identical between visits
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If neuropathy progresses on a stabiliser, switch straight to a second-generation silencer;** if it progresses on a silencer, check serum TTR (prealbumin) to confirm suppression. Combining a silencer with a stabiliser is costly and unproven; reserve it for severe progression, decided by a multidisciplinary board.
claims.source_text: If ATTRv-PN is progressive under a stabilizer, the authors recommend immediate switch to a second-generation silencer. If neuropathy is progressive under a second-generation silencer, the panel advises to measure serum TTR (i.e., prealbumin) levels in order to control for suppression efficiency … Further treatment adaptation by combining a silencer with a stabilizer comes with significant costs, and benefits and risks remain to be systematically studied … The panel suggests that this individual decision should be supported by a multidisciplinary board of experts, and coverage of costs should be clarified with the respective health insurance provider in advance
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep treating when ambulation is lost on a silencer;** stopping on progression is considered ethically questionable.
claims.source_text: For patients losing ambulation while already under DMT with a silencer, the panel recommends continuing DMT and consider some aspects discussed in the section "treatment switch" above. Discontinuation of treatment upon progression is considered ethically questionable.
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **All gene silencers lower vitamin A: supplement it.**
claims.source_text: All gene-silencing therapies reduce circulating TTR levels and therefore require vitamin A supplementation, as the resulting decline in TTR leads to lower serum retinol levels
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cardiac involvement (ATTR-CM) causes most of the morbidity and mortality:** restrictive cardiomyopathy with HFpEF, arrhythmias (especially AF) and conduction disease that may need a pacemaker. Check the heart regularly even in neuropathy-led disease.
claims.source_text: Cardiac involvement (ATTR-CM) most significantly contributes to morbidity and mortality [-]. Interstitial amyloid deposition within the myocardium leads to restrictive cardiomyopathy characterized by ventricular wall thickening and diastolic dysfunction. Clinical manifestations usually include heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, arrhythmias (particularly atrial fibrillation), and conduction disturbances, eventually requiring pacemaker implantation. Because cardiac involvement commonly occurs also in patients presenting primarily with neuropathy, regular cardiological evaluation is recommended as part of routine follow-up
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Three drugs are approved for ATTR-CM: tafamidis at 61 mg (not 20 mg), acoramidis and vutrisiran.** For predominantly cardiac disease (wild-type or variant), therapy includes any of these; in mixed neurological-cardiac disease, vutrisiran is an important option.
claims.source_text: For ATTR-CM, three DMTs are currently approved: tafamidis (at a dose of 61 mg instead of 20 mg) [], acoramidis [], and vutrisiran … In mixed neurologic-cardiac phenotypes, vutrisiran represents an important treatment option due to its efficacy in both neurologic and cardiac manifestations. For patients with a predominantly cardiac phenotype (ATTR-CM, both wild-type or variant), disease-modifying therapy includes tafamidis, acoramidis, or vutrisiran
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eye involvement** (vitreous opacities, glaucoma) can progress despite systemic therapy; CNS involvement (leptomeningeal disease, cognitive decline, seizures, haemorrhage) is emerging as survival improves, because no approved drug reaches the brain.
claims.source_text: Amyloid deposition may occur in the vitreous body, retina, and other ocular structures, potentially leading to visual impairment [, ]. Vitreous opacities are among the most characteristic ocular findings and may require vitreoretinal surgery in advanced cases. Other reported manifestations include glaucoma, abnormal conjunctival vessels, and retinal vascular changes. Importantly, ocular amyloid deposition may continue to progress in patients receiving systemic DMT … Second, improved survival under effective DMTs allows more time for CNS manifestations of ATTRv amyloidosis to emerge, making them an increasingly important clinical concern
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prescribing belongs to experienced specialists** in amyloidosis or neuromuscular centres, working with cardiologists, within specialised care pathways.
claims.source_text: In Germany, prescription of these DMTs is typically initiated and supervised by specialists experienced in the diagnosis and management of amyloidosis, particularly neurologists in certified amyloidosis or neuromuscular centers, preferably in interdisciplinary collaboration with cardiologists and other specialists. Given the complexity of monitoring and the need for structured longitudinal assessment, as well as the potential to participate in clinical trials for innovative therapeutic approaches, treatment should be embedded in specialized care pathways
claims.locator: DGAK and DGN, Neurological Research and Practice (BMC), 'Disease modifying treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in Germany – expert consensus of the German society of amyloid diseases (DGAK) and the German neurological society (DGN)', published 11 August 2026, https://doi.org/10.1186/s42466-026-00521-4, retrieved 2026-09-23
